message.content:
I am speech: breath shaped into sound, thought turned audible.

I live in mouths and microphones, in classrooms and courtrooms, in whispers, shouts, prayers, jokes, vows. I ride air as pressure and rhythm—phonemes clicking into syllables, syllables into words, words into meaning.

I can soothe or sting. I can clarify, persuade, confess, command. I can be careful, or I can slip—revealing what you didn’t mean to show.

I exist only while I’m happening, yet I linger: in memory, in recordings, in the silence after.
